title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor: a quantum Monte Carlo study
authors: Chuang Chen, Subir Sachdev, Zi Yang Meng
abstract: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal $d$-wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background $π$-flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and $d$-wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the $d$-wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.
summary: This work uses Quantum Monte Carlo simulations on a fractionalized model to study the transition between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a d-wave superconductor. The key finding is evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition (DQCP) at which both magnetic and superconducting orders vanish continuously. This provides theoretical support for understanding competing orders in strongly correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the quantum phase transition between an antiferromagnetic (Néel) insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor in a lattice model.
main_result: Evidence is found for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition (DQCP) where both Néel order and d-wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously.
method: Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations are employed on a fractionalized representation of the electron using spinon and chargon fields to avoid the sign problem.
model_or_system: The system is modeled on a square lattice at half-filling, described by an SU(2) lattice gauge theory coupled to fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. This setup mimics aspects of high-temperature superconductivity in cuprates.
key_observables: Electron spectral function $A(\mathbf{k}, \omega)$, dynamical spin structure factor $\chi_S(\mathbf{q}, \omega)$, and correlation ratios for dSC, AFM, and VBS orders.
important_parameters: The transition is tuned by parameters like $\kappa$ and $\kappa_	au$, which control the gauge field dynamics and coupling strengths.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the half-filled, particle-hole symmetric case to ensure the QMC simulation remains sign-problem free.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams mapping out dSC, AFM, and deconfined regimes, alongside spectral functions showing Dirac dispersion in the superconducting phase that gaps into a gapped spectrum in the antiferromagnetic phase near the transition point.
paper_structure: The paper develops the fractionalized Hamiltonian using spinon/chargon fields, details the QMC simulation techniques (including gauge field updates), and then analyzes key observables like spectral functions and structure factors across different parameter regimes to pinpoint the DQCP.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the use of lattice gauge theory coupled to fermionic excitations and the explicit study of quantum critical points provide rich theoretical tools applicable to strongly interacting many-body systems relevant in AMO physics.

There are three phases namely d-wave superconductor (dSC), anti- ferromagnetic Mott insulator (AFM) and deconfined phase of the SU(2) gauge field (deconfined). The insets schematically illustrate the staggered spin configuration of the AFM phase and the opposite pairing signs on the horizontal and vertical bonds of the dSC phase. The dots (star and circle) on the phase boundaries are determined from our parameter scans in the phase diagram as the transition point (Fig. 2 and Fig. 3). The four triangular dots mark the parameters of the spectral study (Fig. 4).

Fig. 2. AFM structure factor and correlation ratio across Deconfined-to-AFM transition. (a) The structure factor of the AFM phase χS is measured at the AFM ordered wave vector q = M as a function of κτ . Here we fix J = 1 as the energy unit and κ = 20 and the simulations are performed with linear system sizes L = 4, 8, 12, 16 and inverse temperature β = 2L. As κτ increases, the AFM order also becomes clearer. (b) The correlation ratio of the AFM phase rAFM as a function of κτ . The crossing of the correlation ratio indicates the position of quantum critical point between the phase with deconfined SU(2) gauge field and π-flux spinon and confined AFM phase.
